answer: Each identity must join the karst trust graph with three disjoint paths to the core. Each path has a distinct endorser locking a 60-unit bond, so one identity costs 180. A prism board publishes the graph; the cut fee rises with newcomer count: the kth newcomer pays 180 plus 10(k-1), so the 1000th pays 10170 and 1000 fakes cost 5175000. An endorser may back only one newcomer per epoch; a second backing triggers a whisper alert freezing both paths for slashing. A rented-endorser ring fails, since its paths converge instead of staying disjoint. An honest agent pays 180 once.
